title: IDEA attorneys’ fees as part of costs
shortTitle: IDEA attorneys’ fees as part of costs
summary: The assigned fee provision permits reasonable attorneys’ fees for qualifying prevailing parents, and the Supreme Court held that it did not authorize expert-consultant fees.
notes:
The controversy concerns how the legal term costs and the reference to attorneys’ fees interact with a conference report describing expert expenses. The Second Circuit regarded the report, related precedent, legislative developments, and educational-access purpose as supporting expert reimbursement. The Supreme Court rejected that construction in Arlington Central.

The Spending Clause majority asked whether the text clearly notified funding recipients of liability for expert fees, while Ginsburg relied on the text without that rationale. This provision record therefore identifies both the governing outcome of the assigned case and the interpretive disagreement; it does not present the superseded Second Circuit result as the rule.
